title: Introduction to Spanish for Heritage Language Learners I
description: First in the sequence of Spanish for Heritage Language Learners track (181, 281, 282, 381). Emphasis on developing listening and speaking skills in the heritage language, understanding and practicing basic grammar, and cultivating positive attitudes towards the heritage language and the heritage culture.
notes: Requires exposure to Spanish in the home and neighborhood in the U.S. Not open to native speakers (with high school diploma from a Spanish-speaking country) or students with credit in SPAN 201, SPAN 202, SPAN 211, SPAN 282, SPAN 301, or higher numbered Spanish course. Replaces SPAN 101 and SPAN 102 for Preparation for the Major. Taught in Spanish. Native speakers of Spanish will not receive credit for taking lower division courses in Spanish except with advanced approval from the department. No credit will be given for lower division Spanish language courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Intermediate Spanish I

title: Introduction to Business Spanish
description: Business vocabulary, basic business and cultural concepts, situational practice to conduct business in Spanish by preparing documents. Grammar review and development of cross-cultural awareness.
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Spanish Civilization
description: Spanish culture of the past and present, with emphasis on literature, philosophy, and the arts.
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Spanish American Civilization
description: Spanish American cultures, with emphasis on literature, philosophy, and the arts.
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Mexican Civilization
description: The major currents and characteristics of Mexican culture, as expressed through the centuries in literature, philosophy, and the arts.
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Advanced Grammar
description: Significant systematic features of modern Spanish grammar. Required for credential applicants.
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

description: Develops oral abilities in diverse registers at advanced level of proficiency. Writing production in critical thinking. Enhances awareness of cultural texts from Spanish-speaking world. Replaces
notes: Not open to students with credit in either

title: Academic Reading and Writing for Native Speakers of Spanish
description: Reading and writing as preparation for advanced academic writing. Readings from a variety of genres to include fiction. Production of expository essays that demonstrate critical competence. Development of linguistic ability and syntactic organization. Transformation of simple, basic structures into complex writing. Replaces
notes: Not open to students with credit in either

title: Spanish Enhancement for Translation and Interpretations
description: Bridges gap between Spanish for communication and Spanish for work. Acquisition of translation and interpretation skills (active listening, text analysis, anticipation, memory, public speaking).
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Introduction to Literary Analysis
description: Literary analysis of narrative, poetry, and theatre of Spanish-speaking world through study of rhetorical devices.
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Spanish Literature and Cultural Studies
description: Spanish writers and works in a variety of literary genres.
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Spanish American Literature and Cultural Studies
description: Spanish American writers and works in a variety of literary genres.
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Advanced Business Spanish
description: Vocabulary and discourse related to business topics and functional areas, goods and services, marketing, finance, foreign market entry, import-export. Geographic literacy and cultural understanding of Spanish-speaking world.
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Spanish for Educators
description: Project-based collaborative analysis of linguistic and cultural competencies in Spanish to interact with K-12 schools and Spanish-speaking communities.
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Spanish for Health Professions
description: Project-based collaborative analysis of cultural and linguistic competencies needed for future health care professionals.
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Spanish for Legal and Criminal Justice Professionals
description: Spanish oral and written communication in criminal justice and legal fields within United States and Spanish-speaking countries. Rule of order terms and court protocols.
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Spanish Linguistics
description: Structural, historical, and applied Spanish linguistics.
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Spanish in the United States
description: Language-related phenomena in Spanish-speaking groups and communities across the U.S. to include dialects, language maintenance, and language use in various sociocultural domains.
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Language Variation in the Spanish-Speaking World
description: Sociolinguistic and pragmatic variation across the Spanish-speaking world. Interactions between identity, language, and society.
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Methods in Teaching Spanish as a Second Language
description: Teaching of Spanish as a second language: contemporary theory and methods. Emphasizes training in teaching techniques to develop students’ presentational, interpersonal, and interpretative skills.
notes: Taught in English and Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish courses.

title: Introduction to Translation Studies
description: Theoretical grounding and practical problems of literary and nonliterary translation; linguistic and cultural obstacles; literary, legal, commercial, medical, social services lexicons in context.
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Translation Theory
description: Historical overview of translation theory. Translation types and conventions. Theoretical considerations of lexical, morphological, verbal, phonic, syntactic, and hermeneutic elements. Cross-language equivalence, fidelity, loss and gain in translation. Criteria for excellence and evaluation. Culture and commerce of translation.
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Advanced Spanish-English/English-Spanish Translation
description: Practicum involving methods and techniques in translation of legal or government papers, banking documents, and business contracts from Spanish into English and from English into Spanish. Practice in translation of old Spanish into English (deeds, surveys, baptismal records, manuscripts of books).
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Selected Studies in Spanish
description: Topics in Spanish or Spanish American language, literature, culture, and linguistics.
notes: See

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.
notes: This course is intended only for students who are currently enrolled in or who already have credit for all upper division courses in Spanish available in any given semester. Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Genre Studies in Spanish Literature
description: A specific literary genre: overview of the genre’s development in Spanish literature (Spanish novel, short story, theatre) or focus on a narrower period (contemporary narrative, modern poetry).
notes: See

title: Genre Studies in Spanish American Literature
description: A specific literary genre: overview of the genre’s development in Spanish American literature (the Spanish American novel, short story, theatre) or focus on a narrower period (vanguardista poetry, the “Boom”).
notes: See

title: Don Quixote
description: A close reading of Cervantes’ novel Don Quixote, Parts I and II.
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Mexican Literature
description: Mexican literature from the Romantic period to the present. Special emphasis placed on contemporary era.
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Consecutive English/Spanish Interpretation
description: Consecutive interpretation techniques focusing on current events to include notetaking technique for interpreters, preparation for meetings, language register, active listening, structure of a speech, abstracting meaning, sight translation in the booth.
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Simultaneous English/Spanish Interpretation
description: Simultaneous interpretation techniques focusing on current events. Simultaneous, whispered, and relay interpretation, preparation for meetings, language register, listening, structure of a speech, abstracting, sight translation in the booth.
notes: Taught in Spanish. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Spanish course.

title: Selected Studies in Spanish
description: Topics in Spanish or Spanish American language, literature, culture and linguistics.
notes: See

title: Seminar in Hispanic Literary Theory
description: Critical issues in Hispanic literary theory. Emphasis on contemporary theory: structuralism, post-structuralism, feminism, cultural studies, and gay and lesbian studies.

title: Foundations and Research Methods of Hispanic Linguistics
description: Morphology, phonology, syntax of Spanish in historic and regional varieties. Qualitative and quantitative research related to sociolinguistics and pragmatics of Spanish, language acquisition, bilingualism, contact varieties. Spanish in teaching and translation.

title: Early Modern Hispanic Literature
description: Philosophic, political, and aesthetic ideas in early modern Hispanic literature. Spanish and Spanish American texts spanning from fifteenth to eighteenth centuries.

title: Spanish Literature: Eighteenth to Twentieth Century
description: Philosophical, political, and aesthetic ideas in literature of neoclassicism, romanticism, realism, and modernism from eighteenth through twentieth centuries.

title: Spanish American Literature: Independence to Present
description: Spanish American literature in its artistic and ideological tendencies from age of independence to present. Literary movements include romanticism, Modernismo, criollismo, and indigenismo.

title: Advanced Topics in Spanish Linguistics
description: Specific aspect of Spanish descriptive, historical, or theoretical linguistics.
notes: See

title: Seminar in Spanish Discourse Analysis
description: Analysis of oral discourse in Spanish. Basic readings in field and strategies to collect and analyze data.

title: Spanish Women Writers
description: Feminist and cultural studies approach to works of Spanish women writers. Analysis of issues on gender, class, race.
notes: See

title: Issues in the Study of Spanish Bilingualism
description: Theories and research on bilingualism with special emphasis on Spanish/English. Definitions of bilingualism. Bilingual typologies. Acquisition of bilingual abilities. Bilingualism and testing. Intersection of bilingualism and translation/interpreting studies. Individual and societal bilingualism.

title: Selected Topics
description: Intensive study in specific areas of Spanish.
notes: See

title: Seminar in Spanish American Literature
description: A genre or movement of Spanish American literature.
notes: See

title: Seminar in Realism
description: Theoretical and historical underpinnings of literary realism. Examines key realist texts from variable periods in Spain or Latin America. Topics include the picaresque novel, naturalism, regional novel, thesis novel, and magical realism.
notes: See

title: Seminar in Spanish American Culture, Film, and Society
description: Works of representative authors and cultural production of Spanish America.
notes: See

title: Seminar in Reading in the Transatlantic Imaginary
description: Exploration and critical analysis of texts produced by authors who lived and wrote between Spain and Spanish-America. Relationship between a cultural text and its place of origin.

title: Applied Spanish Linguistics for Teachers
description: The application of linguistic theory to the teaching of Spanish at the secondary and college levels.

title: Latin American Essay and Critical Thought
description: The study of aesthetics and conceptual tools to analyze the Hispanic Latin American essay canon and their historical context. Learn and apply discursive techniques and rhetoric figures professionally to master its critical, analytical, and writing capacities.
notes: Taught in Spanish for graduate students.

title: Spanish Language Testing
description: Theories and research on language testing with emphasis on Spanish. Types and purposes of language measurement instruments. Characteristics of tests: practicality, instructional value, validity, reliability, test difficulty. Overview of test formats/methods and their consequences.

title: Spanish Language and Society
description: Basic notions of relationship between language and society in Spanish-speaking world. Methodologies applied to data from monolingual and bilingual speech communities. Variationism, ethnography of communication, and sociology of language in Spanish-speaking world.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Thesis
description: Preparation of a project or thesis for the master’s degree.

title: Thesis Extension
description: Registration required in any semester or term following assignment of RP in Course 799A in which the student expects to use the facilities and resources of the university; also student must be registered in the course when the completed thesis is granted final approval.

title: Comprehensive Examination Extension
description: Registration required of students whose only requirement is completion of the comprehensive examination for the master’s degree. Registration in 799C limited to two semesters.
